correctness.rationale: Inductively, each t-step output depends on a q^t-leaf nested NOR tree indexed by an initial suffix ending in an independent length-(d-t) prefix; distinct prefix blocks partition all q^d initial bits. This proves the unique uniform two-cycle, sharp d bound and independent-block binomial uniformity formula. The two-step probability map has precisely the fixed points 0,p*,1 and a critical repeller, with near-endpoint q-th-power contraction; this gives logarithmic-in-d off-critical T and d-O_P(1) critical T. Exhaustive graph simulations, independent NOR-tree truth tables and exact biased weighted enumeration match the formulas for all specified finite instances.

originality.rationale: Distinct from already known de Bruijn incoming-OR first-hitting formulas: alternating NOR creates an unstable nontrivial Bernoulli fixed bias and a sharp change in first-global-uniform-entry time. Pearl (1980) already studies one-root alternating minmax tree probabilities and their rapid convergence, and McIntosh (1991) studies de Bruijn overlap matrices; their separately published claims do not state the exact full-network first-entry distribution. The related directed NOR period-construction results use other digraphs and do not provide this census. Accessible indexed research queries found no claim implying all stated network-level formulas; possible unindexed combination remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier treatment may already combine classical alternating minimax-tree probabilities with de Bruijn prefix partition to obtain the exact full-network first-entry law.
The result is a precise synthesis of two standard structures; significance rests on the network-wide hitting distribution and its probability-scale transition, not the standalone tree recurrence.
No independent expert assessment of mathematical priority was performed.

value.rationale: For the natural q-ary de Bruijn inhibitory dynamics, full-network synchronization is a nonlocal observable. The exact finite labelled first-entry spectrum for all q,d and initial Bernoulli p, coupled to a sharp O(log d) versus d timing transition at one unstable bias, provides a mathematically motivated, reusable temporal-basin benchmark. It is not merely one arbitrary finite count or a reformulation of tree probability convergence.
